definition: Pertaining to the systematic, orderly procedure or design applied in scientific inquiry.
etymology: From New Latin methodologicus, from Ancient Greek μέθοδος (méthodos).
manuscriptExample: Detailed methodological parameters regarding mass spectrometry gradient profiles are provided in Supplementary Methods.
conferenceExample: Reviewer 1 raised a valid methodological concern regarding baseline peptide concentration.

definition: The regulatory adjustment or alteration of biological activity, gene transcription, or signaling pathways.
manuscriptExample: Allosteric modulation of receptor X led to a three-fold increase in downstream cAMP accumulation.
conferenceExample: We addressed whether genetic knockouts resulted in compensatory modulation of related kinase isoforms.
